findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting has no database row
findings.body: The expression execute(...)[0]['id'] assumes the SELECT joining categories to the embed_category site_setting returns a row. Site settings are only stored in site_settings when overridden, and the joined category may also have been deleted, so on a fresh or typical install the result is empty, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError. The migration then fails and blocks deployment/upgrades; the fallback to uncategorized_category_id on line 15 is unreachable in this case.

findings.title: Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim via string-interpolated SQL
findings.body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values are inserted with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) without escaping or the normalization EmbeddableHost normally applies (stripping http://, https:// and paths). A value containing a single quote breaks the SQL or alters it, and values such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares lower(host) to the bare URI hostname, so those migrated rows never match, silently disabling embedding/comment retrieval for previously allowed hosts after upgrade.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
findings.body: The callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!. If an admin API request omits embeddable_host.host (or sends it as null), host is nil and the callback raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of can run. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host passes params[:embeddable_host][:host] straight through, so a malformed create/update returns a 500 rather than a validation error.

findings.title: Update and destroy return 500 for a non-existent host id
findings.body: update (lines 10-11) and destroy (lines 15-16) use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then unconditionally call save_host(host)/host.destroy. For a stale or invalid id (e.g. a host already deleted in another tab) host is nil, producing NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response.

findings.title: Editing a host without a resolvable category crashes the component
findings.body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') with no guard. host.category is undefined when category_id is null, points at the uncategorized fallback the server assigns for blank categories (SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, which save() itself can produce via Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId) returning undefined for a null/unknown id on line 38), or the category was deleted. Clicking edit on such a host throws a TypeError and the row cannot be edited or fixed in the UI.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host makes its category mapping ambiguous
findings.body: The model only validates host format; neither a uniqueness validation nor a unique index (the migration creates the table without one) prevents two EmbeddableHost rows for the same hostname with different categories. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses .first with no ordering, so TopicEmbed.import will non-deterministically file imported topics under whichever duplicate the database returns first, and admins can create conflicting mappings from the new UI.

findings.title: Plural *_ids hydration discards ids and injects undefined entries when a subtype is not embedded
findings.body: For plural associations the new code maps every id through _lookupSubType, assigns the result to obj[pluralized subtype] and deletes the original *_ids key unconditionally. Unlike the singular branch (which only replaces the key when hydration succeeds), if the related collection is absent from the payload/root (or Discourse.Category.findById misses), the array is filled with undefined entries and the original ids are lost, so consumers iterating the association (e.g. embedding.embeddable_hosts) can hit undefined objects instead of simply having no hydrated association.
